ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a sketch map of an island, with a latitude-longitude grid. In the figure, latitude lines marked 17°30′ and 18° can be seen, and the main body of the island is located near these two latitude lines; in the north-south direction, the island body roughly spans the half-degree latitude interval between 17°30′ and 18°, and also extends slightly south of the 18° latitude line. Then reason: The question requires estimating the north-south length of the island, so the latitude difference between the northernmost end and the southernmost end of the island should be read. According to an estimate from the latitude-longitude grid in the figure, the span from the northernmost end to the southernmost end is about 0.7°—0.75° of latitude. Each 1° difference in latitude is about 111 kilometers, so the north-south length is about 0.7×111 to 0.75×111 kilometers, namely about 78—83 kilometers, and rounded it is about 80 kilometers.
